title: A ruled prose PR skips the batch queue and runs only the checks that read its files
why: A prose rewrite of an owner ruling waits hours behind batch CI; main has not moved since 09:09 CST Nov 12.
note: A PR that only rewrites prose to match a ruled store entry skips the batch queue and runs only the checks that read its files. R55 express lane. Kin: ruled-store-one-home. Lane started 14:37 CST Nov 12. Lane 14:39: no R55 express code exists on main or any branch (plan item only); it builds the one home in merge/merge.py, `merge <pr> --confirm --express <ruling-id>`; prose-only means ci-scope.sh turns every flag off on base...head (reused, no checks.yml edit); the batch brake stays (a live batch run refuses: "batch runner cancels it first (R55)"). Store path (triage 14:41 CST): roadmap/rulings/<id>.json on branch roadmap, made by lane ruled-store-one-home at 9bf484366; PR body "Ruling: <id>". R59 (owner 15:05 CST Nov 12, chat: "ruling governs the guard right away"; item 646 closed with the guard option; plan 9064e3c1; home decision owner-override; store entry roadmap/rulings/r59.json): one store, triage writes it from quoted words with their time; an entry naming a guard rule governs that rule at once (the guard lets the ruled act through and names the ruling). Goes express (coordinator 15:06 CST; runner 10 told). Lane 15:33 CST Nov 12 (#2985) asked (a) any ruled prose entry goes express, as built, or (b) only entries naming an express step. Triage: (a). R59 part 5 (owner 15:05 CST Nov 12): "A ruled prose change skips the batch queue"; R55's "a lane outside this list does not take the express lane" is about merge-flow lanes and is older.
